business_problem: Ontada's on-premises data infrastructure and complex warehouse models made it difficult to curate clinical data, enforce PHI governance and share data quickly with partners across the oncology ecosystem.
solution_summary: Ontada adopted the Databricks Data + AI Platform to replace an on-premises environment that made clinical curation, PHI governance and partner data delivery slow and manual. Clinical and operational data from the iKnowMed oncology EHR and other sources are consolidated in one platform, where Ontada can process data once, avoid duplication and automate curation instead of repeatedly moving files through custom warehouse pipelines. Delta Sharing provides governed access, filtering, audits and change tracking so raw and curated datasets can be securely delivered across McKesson's oncology ecosystem and to broader life-sciences partners without rebuilding extracts for every recipient. This architecture shortens request turnaround, reduces storage, compute and labor costs, and gives Ontada a centralized foundation for adding new sources and eventually combining structured and unstructured oncology data as the platform expands.

data_flow: Clinical and operational data, including feeds tied to the iKnowMed oncology EHR, are consolidated into Databricks for curation and governance. Ontada processes the data once, then uses Delta Sharing to distribute raw and curated datasets securely across McKesson and life-sciences partners without recreating extracts for each consumer.
business_outcome: Ontada cut request turnaround from more than eight hours to one hour, saved 25% of employee time by streamlining compliance oversight, reduced data duplication and manual validations, and created a governed sharing model that can scale with data growth across its oncology ecosystem.
